title: Count NULL Values in a Column
description:
A common data-quality check is counting how many rows have a missing value in a column. Use the `COUNT(*) - COUNT(column)` trick to count NULLs.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `manager_id` (NULL for top-level employees)

Return a single value aliased as `null_count` representing how many employees have no manager.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',NULL),(2,'Bob',1),(3,'Carol',1),(4,'Dave',2),(5,'Eve',NULL),(6,'Frank',3),(7,'Grace',2),(8,'Hank',NULL);
solution_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(manager_id) AS null_count FROM employees

test_cases.description: 3 employees have NULL manager_id (Alice, Eve, Hank)

hints: COUNT(*) counts all rows. COUNT(column) counts only non-NULL values. Their difference is the NULL count.
You can also use SUM(CASE WHEN manager_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) for the same result.
explanation: COUNT(*) = 8 (all rows). COUNT(manager_id) = 5 (skips NULLs). Difference = 3, which is the number of NULLs. Employees with NULL manager_id are Alice (id 1), Eve (id 5), and Hank (id 8) — the top-level employees.
